Sean / Monica / Laura — quick triage notes from the edge team:

What we see:
- Spike window: 08:43–09:05 ET with error rate peaking ~11% 502/503 in us-east cluster.
- Load balancer health checks show rapid backend flapping on 3 of 8 edge pods (edge-pod-7/8/9) — rapid termination and restart cycles.
- Autoscaling policy on the edge pool triggered concurrent instance boot followed by traffic redistribution, exposing an unintended race condition in connection draining logic.
- Client retries combined with our lack of short-circuit rate limiting resulted in a retry storm that pushed healthy pools to exhaustion.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:20 ET):
- Disabled autoscaling on affected edge pool and pinned to stable capacity.
- Adjusted LB weight to shift 70% traffic to eu-west and us-west where healthy pools exist.
- Enabled emergency request-rate limiter at the edge to protect inference tier.

Current status (09:29 ET):
- Error rate down to ~1.2% in us-east, checkout success restored for most flows.
- Still monitoring for residual retries and backlog.

Attachments: lb-health-check-logs-20260312.txt, 502-spike-us-east-graphs.png

Next steps:
- Roll back the autoscaling change that introduced the draining race (hotfix in progress, PR referenced below).
- Postmortem and SLO impact analysis.

Markus Klein
Engineering Lead, Edge Services
